hints: Think about what happens to order and movement when liquid water locks into a solid crystal lattice.
Statement 1 is true because ice holds every $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ molecule in a fixed open hexagonal arrangement, while in liquid water the hydrogen bonds are constantly breaking and reforming.
Now link freezing to energy change and to density, remembering that ice floats on water, to decide which two statements work together.
walkthrough:
**Check Statement 1 - Order in Ice vs Water**

In liquid water, molecules move around and hydrogen bonds break and make all the time. In ice, each $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ is hydrogen bonded in a fixed, regular open hexagonal lattice. So statement 1 is correct.

**Check Statement 2 - Energy of Freezing**

Freezing is bond making in terms of intermolecular forces. More hydrogen bonds are formed and held permanently when liquid becomes solid.

Rule to remember:
$$\text{liquid} \to \text{solid : bonds formed, energy released, } \Delta H < 0$$

**Check Statement 3 - Density**

The open lattice in ice actually takes up more space than the jumbled molecules in liquid water. That is why ice is less dense and floats.

So:
$$\text{density of ice} < \text{density of liquid water}$$
This means statement 3, which says the opposite, is incorrect.

**Combine the Conclusions**

Statements 1 and 2 are correct, statement 3 is incorrect. That combination points to the option for 1 and 2 only.

options.A: Incorrect because it includes all three statements. Statements 1 and 2 are correct, but statement 3 is backwards. Ice floats on water, so ice must be less dense than liquid water, not more dense.
options.B: Correct because only statements 1 and 2 are true. Ice has a regular hydrogen bonded lattice, and freezing releases heat so it is exothermic. Statement 3 is false since liquid water is more dense than ice.
options.C: Incorrect because it includes statement 3. Statement 2 is correct as solidification is exothermic, but statement 3 is wrong. Pure liquid water sinks ice, proving water is more dense than ice.
options.D: Incorrect because it includes only statement 1. Statement 1 alone is true, but statement 2 is also true and should not be left out. Freezing forms stable hydrogen bonds and gives out latent heat.
